newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Post-op Yeltsin more active 100 days into new term.
newsitem.headline: Post-op Yeltsin more active 100 days into new term.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who had open heart surgery nearly two weeks ago, was reported at the weekend to be recovering well as he marked the first 100 days of his second term of office.

Doctors said Yeltsin, who has scarcely been in the Kremlin since he was re-elected on July 3, planned to leave the central Moscow hospital where he has been recuperating to take a walk on Sunday outside the Barvikha sanatorium, a few kilometres (miles) away on the outskirts of the capital.

"This morning Boris Nikolayevich not only spoke to us, he got up, shoved all the doctors aside and said: "Look, boys, yesterday I worked and I can walk like this now," Renat Akchurin, the surgeon who led Yeltsin's operation, told a news briefing. Yeltsin then marched across the room, he added.
Journalists later reported seeing the presidential motorcade outside Barvikha but no one at the Kremlin was immediately available to confirm that Yeltsin had gone ahead with his walk.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre, Sergei Mironov, said Yeltsin would start meeting officials next week and would hold talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday.

Chernomyrdin has been given greater powers during Yeltsin's illness, but the Kremlin leader's absence from the political scene has led to fierce infighting within his entourage which flared again last week.
Yeltsin would be moving from the Central Clinical Hospital to Barvikha on Thursday or Friday, Mironov told the briefing for Russian news media.
"The president's recuperation is going well," Akchurin said. "The president is active, Today he is going for a walk at the dacha in Barvikha, to be in normal surroundings for a while."

Akchurin, who led the November 5 quintuple bypass surgery on Yeltsin, said the 65-year-old president had lost weight but had got stronger since the operation, designed to allow him to return to normal life.

Akchurin said scarring on Yeltsin's heart revealed during the bypass surgery had backed up his earlier view that Yeltsin had suffered a third, unannounced heart attack shortly before the presidential run-off.
A Russian newspaper on Saturday published the first picture of Yeltsin since he had the operation to clear the blood supply problems which had led to the attacks.
The photograph in the liberal daily Sevodnya showed a relaxed-looking Yeltsin wearing a patterned cardigan drinking tea with his wife Naina and granddaughter Masha.
Sevodnya said the photograph, released by the presidential press service, was taken on Friday in the hospital.
Later the press service said Yeltsin had worked four hours on Saturday on official papers, one hour longer than on Friday, and had signed a series of decrees.
The picture and reports seemed to be the latest step in the Kremlin's strategy of reassuring the country that Yeltsin was recovering fast and in control of affairs of state.
But some newspapers were sceptical at the weekend after a new scandal broke around his chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais.

"Who are the people at the helm of the country?" a headline in the communist opposition daily Sovietskaya Rossiya said after a newspaper report alleging irregularities in Yeltsin's reelection campaign team.
Both Chubais and his arch-enemy, Yeltsin's former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov, denied any part in the report.

Saturday marked 100 days since Yeltsin's August 9 inauguration, but because of his heart problems he has only been in the Kremlin a few times. Most of his time has been spent in Barvikha, a complex of government rest houses outside Moscow.
Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared, but he did not say when it would be.
